events.description: 23. DOCKET TEXT ORDER: Plaintiff is ordered to respond to 20 MOTION to Stay Briefing re 17 MOTION for Summary Judgment by noon August 18, 2025. Defendant is then permitted to file a reply by noon August 21, 2025. Currently, the pending 17 MOTION for Summary Judgment and 18 MOTION to Dismiss impose overlapping deadlines on the parties under DUCivR 7-1(4)(A)(iii), DUCivR 7-1(4)(B)(iii), and the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure. Therefore, the parties are ordered to meet and confer or separately propose a filing schedule first for resolution of the Motion to Dismiss, and then for the resolution of the Motion for Summary Judgment should Defendant's Motion to Dismiss be denied. The schedule should take into consideration the timeline frames articulated in DUCivR 7-1 and the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure and the parties' mutual desires to resolve this matter in an efficient and timely way. So ordered by Judge David Nuffer on 8/13/25 (docket text only - no attached document) (alt) (Entered: 08/13/2025)

events.description: 25. NOTICE OF DEFICIENCY re 24 Joint MOTION for Scheduling Order. As a briefing schedule setting motion deadlines is not the same thing as a scheduling order setting case-wide deadlines and possible hearing dates, the wrong motion relief was selected. The only motion relief that allows motion briefing deadlines to be set is the "Extension of Time to File Response/Reply". The clerk will correct the motion relief and entry text at this time; however, filers are reminded that the "Scheduling Order" motion relief can only be used when requesting entry of the initial scheduling order for the case. (alt) (Entered: 08/19/2025)

events.description: 36. DOCKET TEXT ORDER: Ordering supplemental briefing. On November 25, 2025, The Tenth Circuit issued a decision in Voter Reference Found., LLC v. Torrez, No. 24-2133 (10th Cir. Nov. 25, 2025). In Torrez, the Tenth Circuit finds that there is standing because of the State's threat of a criminal prosecution and noted that the plaintiff's "claim does not rest on an informational injury." Because the opinion was published after the parties in this case submitted their briefs, the parties have not had the opportunity to discuss the impact on this case. Therefore, supplemental briefing is necessary. As the movant, the Lt. Governor may with 14 days file a supplemental memorandum arguing the impact of Torrez on this case. Although Mr. Lyman submitted a 35 Notice of Supplemental Authority, it fails to address the Tenth Circuit's standing analysis under the NVRA in Torrez. Therefore, within 14 days after that memorandum is filed Mr. Lyman may file a second memorandum regarding standing. After all briefs are submitted, they will be reviewed and considered in the forthcoming order on the Lt. Governor's pending 18 MOTION to Dismiss. So ordered by Judge David Nuffer on 12/5/25 (docket text only - no attached document) (alt) (Entered: 12/05/2025)
